task.name: Stale Documentation Remediation
task.description: Review documentation that has not changed in 180 days and surface only pages whose current repository behavior contradicts their guidance.
task.intent: Reduce maintainer effort spent finding and remediating materially stale documentation without creating duplicate review work.
activationConditions: A tracked documentation page has not changed in at least 180 days.
Current repository evidence materially contradicts the page.
requiredEffects: Each novel stale-documentation finding identifies the page and contradictory repository evidence.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding.
noopConditions: No old documentation contradicts current repository evidence.
Every supported finding is already tracked.
successConditions: Supported findings are remediated or explicitly dismissed within the evidence window.
Duplicate and unsupported findings create no maintainer attention.
uncertainties: File age alone does not establish staleness.
A documentation change may resolve more than one finding.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel stale-documentation findings assigned to the run that are resolved or explicitly dismissed within 30 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported findings it assigns.
acceptedEvidence: A merged pull request that changes the identified documentation page.
A closed finding issue explicitly marked resolved or dismissed by a maintainer.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran.

metric.name: resolved-supported-findings
metric.formula: resolved-or-dismissed supported findings / supported novel findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 30 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned finding set or required repository evidence cannot be read.
